identity.title: Food Safety Plan for Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips

scan.summary: This is the company's Food Safety Plan under the FDA's Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Preventive Controls rule. It describes the hazards in making refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips, the preventive controls to manage them, and how the company monitors, verifies, and records its compliance. The plan is written by a Preventive Controls Qualified Individual and is what the company must follow to keep the product safe and within the law.
scan.freshness_note: The plan is dated May 12, 2025, and is now 16 months old as of September 27, 2026. FSMA plans must be re-evaluated at least once every two years under 21 CFR 121.149, so this plan is not yet due for a mandatory re-evaluation, but you should confirm it has been reviewed by the PCQI quarterly and updated if conditions have changed.

gaps.title: Recall plan not described
gaps.description: The plan does not include procedures for notifying customers, removing product from distribution, and investigating the root cause if a food safety issue is discovered. FSMA requires a recall plan as part of the food safety plan.
gaps.fix: Add a section describing how the company will identify affected product, notify customers and the FDA, remove product from commerce, and investigate what went wrong. Include roles, communications templates, and timelines.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.160(a) requires the food safety plan to include a recall plan

gaps.title: Allergen control for tahini receipt not fully detailed
gaps.description: The plan identifies sesame allergen (from tahini) as a hazard requiring preventive control, and section 8 says tahini comes only from approved suppliers with audit certificates. However, the plan does not specify what the receiving inspection procedure is, what to do if a tahini shipment is mislabeled or the label does not match the purchase order, or how the incoming tahini is verified to be free of undeclared sesame before it enters production.
gaps.fix: Add to section 4 (Preventive Controls) or section 8 (Supply-chain program) a description of the incoming tahini verification procedure: inspect the label against the purchase order and certificate of analysis, verify the sesame allergen declaration, and confirm it matches the expected product. Document this on a receiving log.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.126 requires controls for allergen hazards to include verification of supplier controls
gaps.locator: section 4, Sesame allergen row, or section 8
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: Listeria environmental monitoring frequency may be insufficient
gaps.description: The plan specifies that Listeria spp. environmental swabs are taken at 10 sites weekly in zones 1 and 2. However, the plan does not state how many zones are in the facility or how the swab sites are selected or spaced, and 10 sites per week may not be adequate for a plant with a blending and filling line that is a high-risk area for Listeria post-cook contamination. FDA guidance and FSIS protocols often recommend more frequent or more extensive environmental monitoring for RTE products with Listeria risk.
gaps.fix: Clarify the total number of environmental monitoring zones, describe which 10 sites are swabbed and why (map them), and consider increasing the frequency to twice weekly during production or justifying why weekly is sufficient based on product distribution and any prior Listeria findings. Document this in a facility map or environmental monitoring plan.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.149(f) requires the food safety plan to include verification activities; 21 CFR 121.150(a) requires environmental monitoring for pathogens in RTE products.
gaps.locator: section 4, Listeria in the RTE environment row; section 7, Verification
gaps.quote: Sanitation of food-contact surfaces before each production run and between products; environmental monitoring swabs weekly

gaps.title: No written procedure for PCQI review timeline
gaps.description: Section 6 states that corrective actions are reviewed by the PCQI within seven days, and section 7 states that records are reviewed within seven working days. However, there is no detail on what triggers a review of records outside the routine seven-day cycle (e.g., if a Listeria spp. swab is positive, does the PCQI review immediately or wait until the routine cycle?). The plan should specify whether corrective action investigations are started the same day or if there is flexibility.
gaps.fix: Clarify in section 6 or 7 that corrective action investigations for biological hazards (Listeria, cook failures) start the same working day, while routine record reviews happen within 7 working days. Specify the role of the PCQI in directing investigation and when affected product is released or discarded.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.160 requires the plan to describe corrective actions and verification.
gaps.quote: All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed by the PCQI within seven days.

gaps.title: No direct supplier audit or testing requirement specified
gaps.description: Section 8 requires suppliers to provide a 'current third-party audit certificate' but does not define what 'current' means (e.g., audit valid within 12 months, 24 months?). It also does not state whether the company performs any direct testing of tahini or dry beans (e.g., allergen verification, pathogen testing) or relies entirely on the supplier certificate of analysis.
gaps.fix: Define 'current' as 'audit certificate dated within the past 12 months' or reference the FSMA audit frequency rule. State whether tahini lots are spot-checked for sesame allergen content (e.g., by ELISA or mass spectrometry) or verified only by label review and supplier certificate. If no direct testing, state that and justify reliance on supplier controls.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.126(a) requires allergen controls to include verification that suppliers have controls in place; 21 CFR 121.86 addresses supplier verification generally.
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: Definition of 'approved suppliers' not in the plan
gaps.description: Section 8 says tahini and beans come from 'approved suppliers' and that 'the approved supplier list is maintained by the quality manager.' However, the plan does not describe the criteria for approval, who reviews and approves suppliers, or how often the list is updated. This is important for FDA compliance and traceability.
gaps.fix: Add a statement that approved suppliers are screened based on third-party audit certificate score (e.g., 'A' rating or higher), location, and commodity-specific hazards; that the quality manager maintains and updates the list; and that the list is reviewed at least annually. Consider adding a statement that if a supplier's audit lapses or a batch fails testing, the supplier is removed from the list until re-qualified.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.86 requires supplier verification that includes review of food safety audit results.
gaps.quote: The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality manager.

gaps.title: Blast chiller temperature monitoring may miss early-phase cooling
gaps.description: Section 5 states the blast chiller operator records temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling log. However, section 4 specifies the critical limit is '135°F to 70°F in 2 hours; 70°F to 41°F in 4 hours.' The monitoring procedure does not ensure the product actually reaches 70°F at the 2-hour mark—only that a reading is taken at 2 hours. If the product is still above 70°F at 2 hours, the procedure as written does not clearly require rejection, although section 6 says 'If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded.'
gaps.fix: Clarify in section 5 that the operator records the temperature at the 2-hour point and verifies it is at or below 70°F. If not, the batch is flagged as a corrective action. Consider adding a more frequent check (e.g., at 1 hour and 2 hours) to catch slow cooling earlier, or specify that a continuous temperature data logger is used to confirm the cooling curve meets the critical limit.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.135(a) requires monitoring procedures that ensure critical limits are met during production; 21 CFR 121.140 requires preventive measures for biological hazards.
gaps.locator: section 5, Monitoring; section 4, Spore-former growth at cooling
gaps.quote: The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling log.

gaps.title: No description of corrective action effectiveness testing
gaps.description: Section 6 describes what to do if monitoring fails (e.g., re-cook, re-clean, hold product), but does not state whether re-tests are required to confirm the corrective action was effective. For example, if an ATP swab fails before start-up, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed, but the plan does not explicitly require the re-swab to pass before production starts.
gaps.fix: Add to section 6 that after each corrective action, a re-test is performed (e.g., ATP swab re-tested, product re-run through metal detector with a test piece) and must pass before production resumes or product is released. This confirms the corrective action was effective.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 121.140(a) requires corrective actions to be effective in ensuring the food is safe.
gaps.quote: If an ATP swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts.

5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
